patterns.property: higher-status / in-charge speaker's position is the keyed outcome
patterns.evidence: In every v3 conversation with a status gap (coordinator B, reporter C, adult neighbour D, counsellor E, judge G, older sister H) the senior speaker's plan or ruling prevails, and in the 6 items whose options split by whose position they carry, the key is the senior side: G3 'A judge convinces a student to show the first round' over 'A student convinces a judge...'; D3 newsletter (adult's) over board/flyers (teen's); G1 card (judge's) over notebook / clamp off (student's); B3 'may let him work on repairs after his birthday' over 'stand next to Mr. Dunmow and pass him tools' (teen's wish). Peer sets A and F do not bear on it. Shipped v2 runs the other way: ITL2-D-C-1 (student's garden over staff member's ledge) and ITL2-H-C-2 (student gets the coach to agree) are keyed junior-wins, so across the section it is 6 of 8; within v3 alone it is 6 of 6. The first-plan-vs-replaced draw was varied (first plan wins A,B,D; replaced C,G) but status was not.

patterns.property: purpose stems: 'To suggest...' / 'To explain why...' frames never keyed
patterns.evidence: All 5 purpose items (2 v3 + 3 shipped v2) carry at least one 'To suggest' or 'To explain why' distractor and none is keyed. 'To explain' in 4 items (F4 'To explain why her mom always baked the cake', G4 'To explain why one shoe was left out', v2 D3, v2 F1), key 0; 'To suggest' in 4 items (F4 'To suggest that his family should make her one', v2 A4, D3, F1), key 0. Keys use other verbs: correct, show, say, warn, report. Within v3 alone only 2 items, so the count is across rounds; eliminating the frame removes 1-2 options per item.

patterns.property: intent-next key is the small immediate errand / preparatory step
patterns.scope: kind intent-next (v3; holds in v2 too)
patterns.evidence: 4 of 5 v3 keys are a fetch/drop/tell errand placed before the main activity: B4 'Fetch the tickets so that he can get his table ready' (distractor 'Start writing tickets for people already waiting'), D1 'Drop her school bag at home and then knock' (distractors 'Take the man's beagle out for its first walk', 'Go upstairs with the man right away'), E4 'Tell her injured friend' (distractor 'Find the Kanby counsellor', a real but later step), A2 'round up Alfie and Birdie' (distractor 'write the clues', the main activity). G1 is the exception (the main task itself). A 'later step / jump-ahead' distractor appears in B4, D1, E4 and is never keyed. v2 agrees: ITL2-F-C-3 'Tell the baker to get extra dough ready', ITL2-H-C-4 'Get written approval' (6 of 7 overall).

patterns.property: hedged option is the key when hedges vary
patterns.scope: batch (weak: each hedged key has a hedged twin)
patterns.evidence: B3 key 'She may let him work on repairs after his birthday' (also 'She may ask Mr. Dunmow to train him'); C4 key 'Rust along one edge may have let water damage the contents' (also 'The lid may be stuck'); H4 key 'She doubts her brother would look after her things' (only uncertainty verb). No unhedged key where hedges vary, but on B3 and C4 one distractor is hedged too, so it narrows to two, not one; with strict may/might only it is 2 items, below the 3-item bar.

checked_clean: key length rank (characters): exactly uniform, longest 8 / 2nd 8 / 3rd 8 / shortest 8 of 32; by words key longest (incl. ties) 8 of 30 varying, strictly shortest 6 of 30
intent-next key longest: 3/5 (A2 tie, B4, D1); main-idea key-tail longest 1/5, shortest 2/5 (D3, F1 tie)

key widest/most general: main-idea options share one frame in A3, D3, F1 and largely C3, so breadth does not vary; detail H1 key is the one abstract paraphrase but D4 'art class' vs 'swim camp' etc. are equal breadth: mixed
transcript word overlap: key highest-overlap option 14/32 (incl. ties), lowest 6/32: mixed (above 25% but far below 75%)
prompt word repetition in options: varies in 6 items (D1, F1, G4, H2 etc.), key highest 2/6: mixed

negatives (not, won't, doesn't, without, nobody): varies 6, key 1 (F4 'nobody ever gives her'); distractors C3, E3, F2, G3, H4: near-eliminate but not 0%; v2 key ITL2-A-C-2 'would do little' breaks it across rounds
absolutes (all, only, whole, every, never): varies 3, key 2 (F3 'whole jar', F4 'nobody ever') vs D3 'every door' distractor: mixed
numbers: varies 8, key 4 (C3, C4, E2, H1 yes; B2, F4, G4, H2 no): mixed; C1 numeric set keys the smallest (single item)
contrast words (but, still, instead, rather): varies 6, key 3: mixed

first word / grammatical frame: most items use one frame across all four options (D2 'It got hurt when...', D4 'To pay for... this summer', F2 'He thinks bakery cakes...', E2 'The man had...'); key has a unique first word in 6/32 (B2, B4, C4, D1, E4, G1 by verb choice): mixed
first plan proposed is the outcome: wins A, B, D; replaced C, G; compromise E; undecided F, H: mixed (draw held)
winner = proposer who withstands objection (A, B, D) vs objector with counter-plan (C, E, G): 3/3 mixed
speaker who opens / speaks last prevails: opener wins C, G; loses A, B, D, E: mixed
endings: 6 agree/compromise, 2 undecided (F, H); undecided keyed as undecided (F1 'still thinking about her cake'): not always agreement

main-idea which summary keyed: actual outcome in all 5, incl. the undecided one (F1); an invented never-proposed outcome appears in all 5 (A3 'leave it to their grandmother', D3 'knocking on doors upstairs', G3 'repeat the first round tonight') and is never keyed, but it is only identifiable by listening; no compromise-named option exists to test

mirror-pair rule (key is one of two mutually reversed options): key in pair C3, C4, F2, G3, A3; not in pair A4 ('travelled alone' vs 'came on the train with her dad'), F1 ('buy rice cakes' vs 'bake at home tonight'): 5/7 = 71%, below bar
tone: key positive/cooperative B3, D3, G3; key negative/critical E3 ('unfair to the teammate'), H4 ('doubts her brother'); no stiff/rude/careless tone-built distractors found: mixed
relationship: 'Two X' distractor (B2 'Two old friends at a repair fair', H2 'Two students living in the same university hall') never keyed, but only 2 items

reused key idea across scripts: 'art' keyed in D4 ('an art class') and H3 ('The advanced art course'), H1 also art-related; injury cause in D2/E1 ('fell down the stairs/steps' distractor in both, 'slipped on' keyed in D2 but a distractor in E1): 2 items each, mixed

within-set cross-item cues: G1's options (3 of 4 about showing the first round) cue G3's key; A2 'write the clues' cues A3 treasure hunt; E4 'Kanby counsellor' consistent with E2 key: soft, 2-3 sets, not counted as a tell
per-author: each author has one conversation (4 items); no author's keys share a length rank or frame across all 4 items (e.g. A ranks 4,3,1,2 by chars; H 1,2,4,3)
